clippings.speaker: Federico Fellini
clippings.quote: Marcello can play both very easy and very difficult characters. He has always been kind of a guide through the situation, a witness and a judge at the same time in the story.
clippings.title: Marcello Mastroianni
clippings.context: Said on set at Cinecitta during a Today show interview with Bryant Gumbel, as reported by Maureen Orth.

clippings.speaker: Federico Fellini
clippings.quote: a very normal face, a face with no personality, a face with no expression, a banal face – a face like yours.
clippings.title: Film School: Marcello Mastroianni and Federico Fellini
clippings.context: Fellini's casting pitch to Mastroianni for La Dolce Vita, as retold by Paste; the article does not clearly cite where the words come from.

clippings.speaker: Marcello Mastroianni
clippings.quote: he gave me a script with blank pages. There was nothing on them—only a cartoon Fellini had drawn of a man swimming with a huge penis that reached to the bottom of the sea.
clippings.title: Marcello Mastroianni
clippings.context: Mastroianni recalls arriving at Fellini's seaside villa to read for La Dolce Vita, as quoted by Maureen Orth.

clippings.speaker: Marcello Mastroianni
clippings.quote: Making a movie with Fellini was a non-stop party and as a director he was really easy.
clippings.title: Marcello Mastroianni
clippings.context: Answering Alain Elkann in Paris, asked what he remembers most about Fellini; the interview was dated 15 June 1994 and the page was posted later (2016 per the site).

clippings.speaker: Marcello Mastroianni
clippings.quote: I did those two Fellini films not as an actor but as a man. I took part because I needed, as a man, to realize myself through them. They are the best mirror of my real self.
clippings.title: Interview with Marcello Mastroianni
clippings.context: About his two Fellini films, La Dolce Vita and 8½; the Cinephilia & Beyond page lists it as a 1965 Playboy interview, but I could not see the Playboy original.

notes: Fellini-to-Mastroianni is thin: the Roger Ebert Fellini interview returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl, and the Criterion 1963 Bachmann audio page also 403'd, so I could not verify their Fellini lines. Two Fellini quotes come from secondhand retellings (GQ 1986 and Paste 2024). The Playboy and Paste titles/dates were taken from secondary pages and are not fully confirmed.
